This calculator ONLY covers primary heirs: spouse, children, father, mother. It does NOT account for grandparents, siblings, or other heirs — their presence changes the distribution. Results here are a calculation aid, NOT a religious ruling (fatwa). For real cases, consult a faraid scholar, imam, or sharia notary. The estate divided is the NET estate, after funeral costs, debts, and a bequest (wasiat, max 1/3 of the estate) are deducted.

Recitation rules & what the colors mean
The tajweed rules used to color the Arabic text on the Qur\'an reading screen. Each card\'s color below is the EXACT color shown when tajweed mode is turned on.
A clear bouncing echo on the qalqalah letters when they carry a sukun or occur at a stop (waqaf) at the end of recitation, making the letter sound bounced rather than soft.
A clear, sustained nasal sound on a nun or mim carrying a shadda, held for roughly 2 beats.
A sukun nun or tanwin followed by ba is converted to a mim sound with nasalization — marked with a small mim sign above the letter in the mushaf.
A sukun nun or tanwin is pronounced concealed — between clear and merged — with nasalization, when followed by one of 15 ikhfa letters.
ت ث ج د ذ ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ف ق ك
A sukun mim is pronounced concealed with nasalization when followed by ba — similar to regular ikhfa, but triggered by a sukun mim rather than a sukun nun/tanwin.
A sukun nun or tanwin merges into the following letter with nasalization, when followed by one of these 4 letters.
A sukun nun or tanwin merges into the following letter WITHOUT nasalization, when followed by ra or lam.
A sukun mim merges into the following mim with nasalization, when two mims occur consecutively.
A natural 2-beat elongation on a madd letter (alif, waw, ya) that meets the conditions — with no hamzah or sukun following it.
A madd letter meets a hamzah WITHIN THE SAME WORD, elongated 4-5 beats.
A madd letter at the end of a word meets a hamzah at the START OF THE NEXT WORD, elongated 2-5 beats.
A madd letter meets a letter carrying a sukun or shadda within the same word, elongated a full 6 beats.
A madd letter meets the end of a verse or a stopping point (waqaf) — may be read as 2, 4, or 6 beats depending on the reciter\'s choice.
A connecting hamzah that is ONLY pronounced when starting recitation from that word — skipped (not pronounced) when continuing on from the previous word.
The lam in the definite article "al-" that is not pronounced — its sound merges into the following sun letter (marked with a shadda in the mushaf).
ت ث د ذ ر ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ل ن
A letter written in the mushaf but NOT pronounced at all — e.g. the extra alif after the "waw of the group" (e.g. قَالُوا۟), which is purely a plural marker.
ا (after وا at the end of a word)

All sources are open and bundled at install, except audio. Some Kemenag data below was obtained via third parties, NOT via LPMQ\'s official API (quran-api.lpmqkemenag.id), which requires a written request letter to the Head of LPMQ — that authorization has not been sought. Affected entries are clearly marked below.
risan/quran-json by Risan Bagja Pradana (risanb.com), licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

equran.id API, fetched once at build time then bundled. Their full Terms of Service explicitly permit \"using the API for app development\" — different status than the Kemenag data below. Not explicitly stated: whether permanent offline bundling (vs. live calls) is allowed — confirm with admin@equran.id if certainty is needed.

The adhan-kotlin library by Batoul Apps (solar position algorithms from Jean Meeus\' \"Astronomical Algorithms\"), computed 100% on-device from your exact GPS location. May differ 1-3 minutes from the official per-city schedule at bimasislam.kemenag.go.id: the official schedule uses one fixed reference point plus an elevation correction for the whole city/regency, while this app uses your exact GPS coordinates (more precise for your location, but may differ from the official reference point). To match your local mosque exactly, check your city\'s official schedule or use the minute correction in Notification Settings.

Each method uses the solar angles set by its own authority (Kemenag RI, Muslim World League, Umm al-Qura, ISNA, etc.). The Kemenag angles — Fajr 20°, Isha 18°, +2 min ihtiyat (Sunrise -2), rounded up — are referenced from falakmu.id and NU Online\'s official FAQ, and were verified against bimasislam.kemenag.go.id\'s schedule within a 1-3 minute tolerance.
Quran.com CDN, everyayah.com as fallback. The only data fetched while you use the app.

Quran.com: personal non-commercial use, and their data may ONLY be cached for 7 days unless permitted in writing to keep longer (this app stores it permanently once downloaded) — written permission needed, contact support@quran.com. everyayah.com/VerseByVerseQuran.com: requires a backlink, fulfilled via the two links below.
Beautiful adhan by Adam-synagda, Wikimedia Commons. Dedicated to the public domain (CC0 1.0) — free to use without conditions.
trianbasofi/almatsurat-json by Trian Basofi Rohman, licensed MIT License.

LPMQ Isep Misbah by Lajnah Pentashihan Mushaf Al-Qur\'an (Indonesian Ministry of Religious Affairs) for the Indonesian mushaf, and Amiri Quran by The Amiri Project Authors (SIL Open Font License 1.1) for the Uthmani mushaf.

kodepandai/colorful-quran (MIT license on the repo\'s CODE, NOT on the Kemenag data inside it). The original data comes from quran.kemenag.go.id, not the official LPMQ API — see the permission note above. Validated across 6,236 verses, 0 out-of-bounds indices.
semarketir/quranjson (MIT). Validated across 6,236 verses, 0 out-of-bounds indices.

renomureza/quran-api-id (MIT license on the repo code), data scraped directly from quran.kemenag.go.id via a third-party script — not the official LPMQ API. Same as the other Kemenag entries, bundling permission has not been sought. Validated across 6,236 verses, 114 surahs.
What if the audio server goes down?
Only new audio downloads are affected. All text and schedules are stored in the app since install, and audio you already downloaded still plays.
